title: Best GPS Watches for Running and Swimming
excerpt: GPS watches for runners who swim: Garmin Forerunner 970 and 570, Suunto Race 2, Coros Pace 4 and Pace 4 Pro, compared on battery, price and maps.
body:
Best GPS Watches for Running and Swimming

Updated November 2026. Prices are US list prices (MSRP) at the time of this update; retailers often sell for less.

Every watch here tracks running, pool swimming and open-water swimming. The real differences are battery life, maps, music and price. Prices are US list prices (MSRP), and battery figures are the manufacturers' ratings.

The picks

Garmin Forerunner 970: most complete

The Garmin Forerunner 970 lists at $749.99. It's rated for 26 hours in GPS-only mode and has offline maps, music storage and multi-band GPS. It suits triathletes who want one watch for training, racing and navigation.

Suunto Race 2: long battery with maps

The Suunto Race 2 lists at $499 in steel. Suunto rates it for 55 hours of continuous dual-frequency GPS, and it supports offline maps. That makes it a strong fit for long-course triathlon and mountain running.

Coros Pace 4 Pro: battery and storage for less

The Coros Pace 4 Pro lists at $449. It's rated for 60 hours of GPS and has 32 GB of storage for MP3 files and maps.

Garmin Forerunner 570: Garmin features without maps

The Garmin Forerunner 570 lists at $549.99. It's rated for 18 hours in GPS-only mode and has multi-band GPS and streaming music, but no offline maps.

Coros Pace 4: best value

The Coros Pace 4 lists at $249. It's rated for 41 hours of standard GPS, and it has dual-band GPS and an AMOLED screen.

What to look for

  • Water rating: check that the watch is rated for swimming, not just splashes. All the watches above are designed for pool and open-water swimming.
  • Battery for your longest race: estimate your finish time, add a margin, and compare it with the watch's GPS rating.
  • Open-water GPS: GPS can't reach the watch underwater, so open-water distance is pieced together from moments when your wrist is above the surface. Dual-band GPS helps, and so does swimming in a straight line.
  • Pool length: enter the correct pool length before you start, because pool swims are counted in lengths, not GPS.

FAQ

What is SWOLF?

SWOLF adds your stroke count to the seconds a length takes, giving a single efficiency score. Lower is better. Compare your own scores over time, at the same pool length.

Do I need a triathlon watch for running and swimming?

No. Any watch with swim tracking will do. Triathlon-focused watches add multisport race modes and longer battery.
